answer: Yes. The story uses metaphor and allusion to expose the fragility of Q’s effortless superiority. Calling the narrator his “Boswell” establishes an admiring chronicler, while relationships dissolving into “nostalgic mist” captures Q’s talent for evading accountability. Meredith’s discovery that “a cathedral was made of styrofoam” crystallizes his hollow grandeur. The final image of uniform gravity turns his humiliation into the narrator’s recognition that Q, too, is subject to ordinary human limits.
